# Workflow notes

The depth behind the one-line comments in `ci.yml` and `schemas.yml`.

## ci.yml

### permissions

`checks: read` — go-toolchain@v1's embedded no-all-builds-job guard scans the head commit's check runs and fails closed without this grant.

`deployments: write` + `artifact-metadata: write` — go-toolchain@v1's publish step registers each release: a GitHub Deployment, and a record on the org's linked artifacts page. Both were warnings until recently and are now hard failures ("Resource not accessible by integration" / HTTP 404), so a build cannot finish without these.

### dashboard-assets

The dashboard's generated bundle, regenerated from source and compared to what is committed. `assets/timeline.js` is embedded via go:embed and is authoritative for the Go build, so it stays committed — this job exists so it can no longer silently DRIFT from `ts/`. Editing `ts/` and forgetting to regenerate used to ship a stale dashboard with a green build; now it is a red one, with the exact command to fix it.

ts0 comes from buildhost as the prebuilt platform-neutral `ts0.cjs` — stock Node and nothing else: no npm, no node_modules, no git (the same shape as the dats job's prebuilt download).

PIN: `?v=N` is an immutable release; `?branch=master` moves on every ts0 merge and would make this gate flap. `v=10` is the current master build — verified to regenerate the committed bundle byte-for-byte. Newer version NUMBERS exist (11, 12) but are builds of ts0 feature branches, not master, so do not bump to a number just because it is higher: resolve `https://dl.pazer.build/ts0?branch=master&os=linux&arch=amd64` and read the `v=` it redirects to, then re-run this job to confirm the bundle is unchanged.

Slim fleet on purpose: this needs Node, curl and network — no docker, no bubblewrap, so none of the dind reasoning below applies.

ts0 is saved as `.cjs` deliberately: the bundle is CommonJS, and a `.js` file would be mis-parsed as ESM if it landed in a `"type": "module"` package. There is no smoke-test step — ts0 has no `version` subcommand (it prints "Unknown command" and exits 0, so such a step proves nothing); the build itself is the check that it runs.

The build step type-checks `ts/` (`testjs/` is excluded — it is run by node's type-stripping runner, which never type-checks, so it has never been under a checker) and rebuilds `assets/timeline.js` in place.

### test

wow-dind, not wow-linux: go-toolchain runs a `.dats` phase (it bootstraps dats and executes `dats/*.dats` as part of this job — "Running dats suites" in the log), and dats SANDBOXES TEST COMMANDS BY DEFAULT, failing a run outright when no backend is usable. The slim fleet can provide neither backend: docker is deleted from that image by design, and bubblewrap needs an unprivileged user namespace a stock container is refused (measured inside a real wow-linux runner: `unshare -U` blocked, `Seccomp: 2`, `CapEff: 0`). Making it work there would cost `seccomp=unconfined` + `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` — most of `--privileged`, on the image whose whole point is being locked down — so the operator's ruling (2026-07-26) is that dats jobs come here instead, where bubblewrap is installed and measured working. See the webhooks repo, `src/hooks/gha-runner/CLAUDE.md`.

The committed dashboard bundle (`assets/timeline.js`) and the committed component `.d.ts` pair (`ts/js-snippets/`) are regenerated by the `//go:generate` directive in `internal/server/dashboard/dashboard.go`, which runs `generate-timeline.sh`: curl a pinned ts0 from buildhost + the component's `.d.ts` pair from js-snippets' Pages, then `node ts0.cjs build` — no npm/npx, no git auth; Node 22 via setup-node. `generate:` is the approval hash for that directive (a bare `go-toolchain` run prints the new one after any directive edit). The freshness gate then fails CI on any diff, so the bundle and the fetched declarations can't go stale — and an upstream component API change turns CI red here instead of drifting.

go-toolchain@v1 itself cache-uploads its `build/` outputs under the `go-build` name on EVERY run (its own composite "Hand off build outputs" step, artifact-free; cache storage is free, artifact storage is billed). That single central hand-off feeds BOTH downstream jobs — the e2e job and publish-ghcr's reusable workflow — which only cache-download it. So this workflow adds NO explicit cache-upload of its own: a second same-run upload of `go-build` would collide on the shared, non-job-disambiguated key (`cache-xfer-go-build-<run_id>-<run_attempt>`) and fail the job. Do NOT re-add an explicit `cache-upload go-build`.

`os:`/`arch:` pin native binaries per platform, NOT the default single fat APE: bbolt memory-maps the run store and does not build against the cosmopolitan libc (undefined: `unix.Mmap`, `syscall.MADV_RANDOM`). Setting `os` or `arch` is what switches the APE back off.

### e2e

Dashboard client harnesses: drive the real committed assets (`dashboard.js` — the push-first section feed; `timeline.js` — the stream-vouched trailing-coverage claims) in vm sandboxes. Authored in TypeScript and run DIRECTLY via node's native type-stripping — no build step, and no committed generated `.mjs` (see `.gitignore`; the repo commits `.ts` source only). The shell glob picks up every `testjs/*.test.ts` (node's bare-directory form is not portable across 22.x). setup-node pins a Node new enough to strip types.

The cache-download restores the binary go-toolchain@v1 handed off in the test job through the actions cache (its central `go-build` upload — go-toolchain uploads its `build/` dir as `go-build`, so the contents restore into `build/` here; exec bit + basename preserved). It fails loudly if the hand-off is missing.

The e2e harness runs `./build/webhook-runner`; the hand-off carries the platform-suffixed build name, so the staging step gives it the unsuffixed name the test expects (mirrors the old `download-exe` `files:` mapping).

The sops e2e tests decrypt `e2e/hooks/sops-hook/secrets.sops.env` with the committed test-only age key.

### dats

Black-box CLI-contract tests (`dats/*.dats`, run by the org's dats test runner) against the real built binary — docker-free, offline, no secrets; see CLAUDE.md "CLI contract tests". wow-dind for the same reason as the test job: dats sandboxes by default and the slim fleet can supply no backend.

The cache-download restores the binary go-toolchain@v1 handed off in the test job (the same central `go-build` upload the e2e job restores).

The suites exec `"${GO_TOOLCHAIN_DATS_BUILD_DIR:-build}/webhook-runner"`; that env var is unset here, so they fall back to `build/`. The hand-off carries the platform-suffixed build name, so the staging step puts the unsuffixed name beside it.

dats itself is a prebuilt binary from buildhost (public download). It is installed into `build/` so the single PATH prepend covers both binaries — no sudo, works on any runner.

### fleet-compat

Would deploying THIS binary break the fleet that is actually running?

It checks TWO trees, because a manifest contract has two sides and a coordinated change moves both:

- webhooks MASTER, the tree deployed right now. A binary that cannot load it is not deployable ON ITS OWN.
- the webhooks branch with THIS BRANCH'S NAME, when one exists: the tree this change is paired with. webhooks CI already builds the runner from its own matching branch, so this is the same convention read from the other end, and it is what a coordinated pair is actually going to be after both merge.

THE GATE: the paired tree must load. If master does not, that is reported as the deploy ORDER (merge webhooks first), not as breakage — because the runtime now makes the wrong order SAFE rather than catastrophic:

- a binary that cannot load the deployed tree REFUSES TO START (`internal/cli.buildLoadAndApply` returns an error and serve exits non-zero), so the image rollout fails visibly and the previous container keeps serving. It never comes up serving a fraction.
- a tree the running binary cannot load is REFUSED and ROLLED BACK (`internal/reloadgate.applyOrRollbackLocked`), so the fleet keeps running the commit it was running and the deploy is held.

That is why this job no longer has to be red to keep the fleet safe. It used to be the ONLY thing standing between a contract change and a silent fleet-wide outage, so it had to red every coordinated pair until the other repo merged — which meant shipping red PRs with a merge-order runbook attached. The runtime owns that safety now; this job's job is to tell you what you are about to deploy, and to fail when NOTHING can serve the change.

Unentitled callers get HTTP 200 + `{}` from secret-server, so an absent token exports as empty rather than erroring. Skipping the check there would turn "could not verify" into a green tick — the deceptive pass this gate exists to prevent. Fail instead.

The paired-tree checkout is `continue-on-error`: a missing branch is the normal case (a runner-only change) and is not an error.

`validate` is docker-free: it loads and checks manifests, builds nothing.

### publish-ghcr

Builds the Dockerfile from the `go-build` hand-off (the reusable workflow cache-downloads `go-build` into `build/`) and pushes `ghcr.io/wow-look-at-my/webhook-runner:latest`. The push itself is gated to master by the reusable workflow's push-branch default, so on feature branches this job just BUILDS the image as a Dockerfile-validation gate and never pushes — no unintended GHCR pushes from PRs. The deployed compose pulls this image; the push notifies docker-updater (GitHub package webhook).

The reusable workflow's optional `updater-webhook-secret` notify is intentionally unwired: docker-updater is notified by the container push itself (GitHub package webhook on the GHCR push), so the CI-side notify is redundant here. Pass `updater-webhook-secret` if that ever changes.

## schemas.yml

Deploy workflow — the master-only branch filter STAYS (org rule: deploy/publish workflows keep their triggers; only pure CI uses bare `on: push`).

The hook.json + concurrency.json schemas used to deploy to GitHub Pages, but GH Pages deploys ride Actions artifacts and the org's artifact storage quota is exhausted — the Pages deploy has failed since 2026-07-17 ("Artifact storage quota has been hit"), freezing the published schema at its 07-15 content. Operator directive 2026-07-19: use buildhost. `buildhost-publish-site` PUTs one tar.gz straight to sites.pazer.build (GitHub OIDC auth, project auto-provisioned) — no Actions artifacts anywhere.

webhook-runner is a private repo, so its buildhost project is private; `public: true` (the `X-Public-Site` mechanism PR previews use) opens just this one site branch for anonymous reads — release artifacts and the rest of the project stay gated. Canonical schema URLs:

- `https://sites.pazer.build/webhook-runner/branch/master/hook.schema.json`
- `https://sites.pazer.build/webhook-runner/branch/master/concurrency.schema.json`

The legacy GitHub Pages site keeps serving its last-published (07-15) content — nothing is deleted here — and hook.json files may keep the legacy github.io URL in `$schema` (the runner only requires `$schema` presence, never a specific URL).

Staging: only `schema/*.schema.json` is published, flat at the site root. The old workflow uploaded the whole `schema/` directory, which also published `schema_test.go` to the public site — fixed here. Every staged file must parse as JSON and carry `$schema` + `$id`.
